title: Aerated Monsoon Slovakian Rice Pilaf
description: A grassy, aerated, and creamy rice dish inspired by the flavors of Slovakia, perfect for a monsoon day.

ingredients.name: Double cream
ingredients.notes: Heavy cream can be used as a substitute.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Use filtered water for best results.

ingredients.name: Grassy Slovakian herb blend (e.g. parsley, dill, tarragon)
Butter
ingredients.notes: Use salted or unsalted, soft or salted.

ingredients.name: Paprika
ingredients.notes: Optional, but adds a smoky flavor.

instructions: Heat the butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the crushed garlic and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the grassy Slovakian herb blend and cook for another minute, until the aroma fills the air.
Add the basmati rice and cook, stirring constantly, for 2-3 minutes, until the rice is lightly toasted.

Add the water, double cream, salt, and paprika (if using) to the skillet. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 18-20 minutes, or until the liquid has been absorbed and the rice is cooked through.
Fluff the rice with a fork and stir in the fried shallots (if using).
Taste and adjust the seasoning as needed.
Transfer the rice to a wooden board and garnish with chopped fresh parsley.
